finding.root_cause: The Windows Celery thread pool invoked get_or_create_event_loop from different task threads. Each thread could create and install a different event loop, while the process-global Celery AsyncEngine/session factory and Redis async client remained initialized against an earlier loop. A later task could therefore check out asyncpg connections or await Redis futures owned by another loop.
observed_errors: got Future attached to a different loop
asyncpg InternalClientError: got result for unknown protocol state 3

lifecycle_before.task_execution: A stopped or newly created event loop was selected from the calling Celery thread and run_until_complete executed the task coroutine.
lifecycle_before.database: A process-global pooled Celery AsyncEngine/session factory survived across task-thread event loops.
lifecycle_before.redis: A process-global async Redis client survived across task-thread event loops.
lifecycle_before.overlap_risk: Windows worker_concurrency=4 allowed different task threads to replace the module-level loop reference while shared async resources remained bound to an earlier loop.

lifecycle_after.strategy: Option A - worker-scoped persistent event loop
lifecycle_after.task_execution: One dedicated daemon thread runs one asyncio event loop continuously per Celery worker process. Celery task threads submit coroutines with asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe.
lifecycle_after.database: The Celery-specific pooled AsyncEngine and async session factory are created on the persistent worker loop, record process/loop ownership, reject incompatible-loop reuse, and are disposed on that loop during worker shutdown.
lifecycle_after.redis: The async Redis client is initialized on the persistent worker loop, records process/loop ownership, refuses reuse by replacing an incompatible client context, and is closed on the owner loop during worker shutdown.
lifecycle_after.fastapi_resource_separation: Celery task stages continue to receive Celery manager sessions explicitly. The FastAPI global engine is not selected for extraction, persistence, mapping suggestions, or XBRL task execution.
lifecycle_after.task_overlap_decision: Task submissions may overlap, but all async work and shared async resources execute on the same event loop. Separate SQLAlchemy sessions remain per task; no concurrency=1 workaround is required.

mapping_suggestion_failure_isolation.extraction_status: REVIEW remains preserved after successful row persistence
mapping_suggestion_failure_isolation.error_metadata: Existing ai_mapping_last_error_message now carries a stable bracketed error code. Loop mismatch and asyncpg protocol-state errors use async_resource_loop_mismatch.
mapping_suggestion_failure_isolation.fine_batik_impact: The Job 51 behavior remains intentionally isolated: its 107 persisted rows and REVIEW status are retained if advisory mapping suggestions fail. The failure is recorded separately and does not dispose, replace, or poison the worker-loop database resources used by Job 52 or Job 53.

checks: All three jobs reach REVIEW without restarting Celery between jobs.
All three jobs persist more than zero extracted rows.
Mapping suggestions complete or fail independently without changing REVIEW.
The third job submits to Azure DI normally.
Worker logs contain no different-loop or asyncpg unknown-protocol-state error.
